title: Minimax Treatment Lotteries under a Root-n Vanishing Kullback-Leibler Penalty

proof_attempt_summary: D0 established a small-positive-penalty symmetric-pair saddle, its support-location elbow and second-order value correction, a uniform local-game bridge, and finite value certificates. The D0.5 math panel passed, but the cold referee assessed only subfield novelty against the field floor. The moderate-penalty support map, exact H=2,c=1 saddle, and continuum off-support certificate remain open; the rubric panel also left a presentation-only ballast finding unrepaired.
tldr: When both treatment contrasts and the Kullback--Leibler penalty are of order \(n^{-1/2}\), the lottery-improvement problem has a nonquadratic bounded-normal decision limit. For each fixed \(H\) and sufficiently small positive \(c\), the exact minimax rule is the symmetric-pair logistic--tanh Bayes rule. Its support location has a sharp three-regime elbow: \(a_c=H\) when \(H<a^\star\), \(a_c=H=a^\star\) at the boundary, and, when \(H>a^\star\), a unique \(a_c=a^\star+\beta c^2+o(c^2)\) with the proved positive coefficient \(\beta\). The uniform bridge transfers the Gaussian minimax value and a generic attaining observed-data sieve uniformly over \(c\in[0,C]\); it does not extend the analytic pair saddle beyond the small-penalty region. The finite convex program gives convergent two-sided value certificates, not exact moderate-penalty support. The set \(S_H\) consists of positive penalties admitting a symmetric-pair saddle, and \(c_{\mathrm{tr}}(H)=\sup S_H\) is only its pair-saddle supremum. Whether \(S_H\) is an interval, whether this supremum is finite and attained, whether pair saddles re-enter, the post-endpoint support geometry, and the exact \(H=2,c=1\) saddle all remain open. This binary model is a transparent benchmark, not a reanalysis of a multivalued savings application.
gap: Fang, Ridder, and Xie analyze a fixed positive Kullback--Leibler penalty, while Hirano and Porter analyze the discontinuous unpenalized treatment boundary. Neither result covers the critical sequence \(\lambda_n=c/\sqrt n\), where the oracle action remains smooth for \(c>0\) but converges to a sign rule at \(c=0\).
fill: The paper proves the entropy-specific small-\(c\) saddle, isolates the exact critical-radius boundary contact and value expansion, matches the Gaussian value with an all-rules local minimax lower bound and a uniformly attaining observed-data rule on \(n\ge\lceil(H/\eta)^2\rceil\), and computes the remaining game through a finite convex program with explicit approximation error.
